content:
Facts: The spouse and children of a predeceased sister of the testatrix challenged a will favoring the testatrix’s siblings, alleging nullity and infringement of their inheritance rights, and sought monetary reinstatement and damages.
Legal framework
Articles 536, 553–564, 591, 624 of the Italian Civil Code on forced heirs, reduction, acceptance with benefit of inventory, and testamentary incapacity or error; Articles 467–468 ICC on succession by representation; Articles 96 and 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure on standing and aggravated liability.
Interpretative issue
Whether relatives succeeding by representation to a sibling of the deceased qualify as forced heirs entitled to bring an action for reduction, and whether generic pleas of testamentary nullity may later be specified into distinct grounds of invalidity.
Principle applied
Only persons expressly identified by law as forced heirs have standing to bring an action for reduction; siblings of the deceased are not forced heirs, and their descendants succeeding by representation lack standing to claim infringement of reserved shares, also requiring prior acceptance with benefit of inventory. Generic allegations of testamentary nullity do not cover distinct grounds such as incapacity or error, which must be timely and specifically pleaded, failing which they amount to an inadmissible mutatio libelli. The manifest groundlessness of an action brought without due legal diligence justifies a finding of reckless litigation and an award of aggravated liability damages under Article 96 CPC.
